main.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup
Asset type: high-fidelity Windows 11 desktop application refactor concept, landscape 16:10.
Primary request: design the proposed Android Webcam Manager with a large integrated camera preview and its own virtual camera and microphone. Render one complete desktop app window, front-on, very crisp readable typography and realistic polished native Windows controls. This is a design proposal, not evidence of a working build. Place a subtle caption outside the app: "REFRACTOR CONCEPT — ILLUSTRATIVE STATE".
Visual design: calm dark charcoal panels, subtle borders, Segoe UI typography, restrained soft blue accents, clear hierarchy, ample spacing. No futuristic glow or dashboard clutter.
Layout: title bar "Android Webcam Manager" with native window controls. Compact header shows a selected device dropdown "Pixel 10 Pro XL", small "USB · Authorized" status and a Settings icon. Central left area about two-thirds width contains a large 16:9 integrated preview showing a naturally lit desk with a small green plant and a book (illustrative camera subject; no faces); clean preview, no separate scrcpy window or captured desktop. An unobtrusive badge at the preview top says "Live". A thin row below the preview reads "Camera receiving · 1920 × 1080 · 30 fps" and offers "Hide preview"; hiding preview does not stop output.
Right column is a coherent control panel: camera dropdown "Rear camera · ID 0"; quality selector with three compact choices "Standard", "Detail", "Motion" and Standard selected; a selected profile description "1080p · 30 fps"; dropdown "Orientation" set to "Landscape"; unchecked checkbox "Mirror output"; Phone microphone toggle enabled; live microphone meter clearly labeled "Phone signal"; subtle secondary link "Advanced settings". Only real controls, no exposure, HDR, focus or decorative unsupported sliders.
Bottom area is one horizontal output card headed "Use in Discord", with two labeled rows: "Camera" then "Android Webcam Camera" and a small "Copy name" button, then "Input device" then "Android Webcam Microphone" with a small "Copy name" button. Include a tiny note "Exact device names shown after installation." Put a visible secondary button "Test inputs" and a muted status "Receiver not checked" nearby; do not imply Discord has been verified.
Bottom-right has a single primary action "Stop streaming" in restrained blue because the illustrated state is active; compact status "Camera streaming · Microphone streaming". Bottom-left a collapsed "Diagnostics" disclosure. The main page must have no OBS setup, cable routing, audio output endpoint selection, command line, recording, account, advertisements, or separate Preview and Start actions.
Constraints: consistent typography, perfectly aligned controls, high legibility at ordinary desktop scale, desktop design not mobile. Avoid duplicate Stop buttons, giant device serials, false 4K output labels, browser chrome, floating preview windows, fancy effect toggles. Show all important controls without scrolling. Make a buildable C/Win32 UI concept with simple rounded rectangular panels. No transparency.

setup.prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup
Asset type: companion high-fidelity Windows 11 desktop setup screen concept for Android Webcam Manager, landscape 16:10.
Primary request: a polished, buildable first-run setup screen for a C Windows app that owns a virtual camera and a virtual microphone driver. It should make setup straightforward with one installation action, and never start phone capture automatically.
Style: native Windows desktop window, dark charcoal panels, restrained soft blue accent, Segoe UI, crisp large legible text, simple aligned controls and spacious layout. Same visual family as a calm dark Android Webcam Manager streaming view.
Caption outside the app "SETUP CONCEPT — ILLUSTRATIVE STATE".
Title bar "Android Webcam Manager". Screen title "Set up your camera and microphone". Subtitle "Install the app's Windows inputs once, then choose your phone and start."
Main area is a clean two-column layout. Left card heading "Windows inputs", with two rows: camera icon, "Android Webcam Camera", amber status "Not installed"; microphone icon, "Android Webcam Microphone", amber status "Not installed". A short paragraph below: "Windows will request administrator permission to install the signed components. Everyday use runs without admin." Prominent shield button "Install outputs". Tiny subdued line "Nothing is recorded. Phone capture stays off."
Right card heading "Phone and capture tools"; row with green check "scrcpy + ADB detected" and detail "scrcpy 5.0.1"; row with green check "Pixel 10 Pro XL" and detail "USB · Authorized"; secondary text button "Choose tool folder"; secondary text button "Connect another phone". A compact helpful tip "Keep USB debugging enabled and allow the phone's authorization prompt."
Below cards, a calm horizontal explanation with three small labeled stages connected by arrows: "Phone" -> "App-managed inputs" -> "Discord or another app". Below: "After installation, the app shows the exact camera and microphone names to select." No default-device switching.
Bottom-left collapsed "Setup details", bottom-right a disabled gray "Continue" button with caption "Install outputs to continue".
Constraints: no OBS, no VB-CABLE, no Windows Volume Mixer, no pairing-code input on this main screen, no accounts, no recordings, no unverified success banner. Do not draw a UAC prompt. Show one installation button, all content visible without scrolling. This is a planning mockup; no real driver installation has happened. Use only the specified meaningful controls. No decorative sliders or invented metrics.
